data.name: UserGuide_ResidentSignInDetails
data.value: Residents sign in with their registered mobile number and personal PIN. Access is limited to an active resident role and the apartment occupancy assigned to that account.

data.name: UserGuide_AdminSignInDetails
data.value: Building administrators sign in with their registered mobile number and PIN. The account is authorized only for its assigned building scope and permissions.

data.name: UserGuide_SuperAdminSignInDetails
data.value: SuperAdmins sign in with an allow-listed email address and password. If two-factor authentication is enabled or required for the account, complete the authenticator challenge before the session is issued.

data.name: UserGuide_MultipleRolesDetails
data.value: A person may be a resident in one apartment and a building administrator in one or more buildings. Select the intended role and scope when prompted. Resident access remains apartment-scoped; administrator access remains building-scoped. The system must not merge these scopes or create duplicate identities just to represent another role.

data.name: UserGuide_IdentityGovernanceDetails
data.value: Resident access depends on a verified identity, an active occupancy, a valid role assignment and a unique registered phone number. Accounts awaiting review cannot sign in. Initial or recovery PINs must be replaced when prompted. Never share a PIN, recovery code or authenticator secret.

data.name: UserGuide_TwoFactorDetails
data.value: Where enabled for an administrator account, use a current code from your authenticator app after entering the password or PIN. Recovery codes are single-use; store them securely offline and do not send them to support.

data.name: UserGuide_ImpersonationDetails
data.value: Authorized administrators may temporarily enter a permitted resident or building context to investigate an issue. The banner identifies impersonation mode. Use Back to my account to restore the previous identity; nested sessions return one level at a time. Actions remain subject to scope checks and audit logging.

data.name: UserGuide_ReceiptImagesDetails
data.value: A receipt image helps extract candidate details such as amount, date, reference and transfer status. OCR is an aid only: it can misread compressed, cropped, rotated or low-quality images. A recognized success message is not proof of settlement. The authorized administrator must verify the transfer against trusted payment evidence before confirming a deposit.

data.name: UserGuide_ReceiptImageQuality
data.value: How to capture a readable receipt

data.name: UserGuide_ReceiptImageQualityDetails
data.value: Upload the original screenshot or image at its clearest available resolution. Keep the full transaction details, amount, currency, date, reference and status visible. Avoid glare, blur, heavy compression, filters and tight crops. For camera photos, keep the phone parallel to the screen or paper, use even lighting and avoid reflections. Do not edit amounts or transaction details.

data.name: UserGuide_DepositHistoryDetails
data.value: New deposits remain pending until an authorized administrator reviews and confirms them. Confirmation, cancellation and reversal are separate financial states. Historical records and available receipt links remain available in the relevant wallet or statement views; a receipt image alone does not post money to the ledger.

data.name: UserGuide_InvoiceQRDetails
data.value: Issued invoice PDFs include a signed QR verification link. Scanning it opens a public verification page that shows limited invoice facts, such as building, apartment number, period and issue date. It does not expose resident contact details or account balances. An invalid signature or unknown invoice is rejected.

data.name: UserGuide_AuditLogsDetails
data.value: Audit logs record important user and financial actions; application logs help diagnose runtime issues. Results are restricted by the viewer's permitted building or apartment scope, and sensitive values are redacted. Use the correlation ID when reporting an issue. Logs support investigation but do not replace source financial documents.

data.name: UserGuide_BackupRestoreDetails
data.value: Create and retain backups before major changes. Review the restore preview and selected collections carefully. A restore session is tied to the previewing account, expires, is single-use and validates the reviewed archive digest before applying changes transactionally. Restore only after an authorized review and against the intended environment; never experiment on production.

data.name: UserGuide_FinancialPeriodsDetails
data.value: Financial entries belong to a defined building and period. Closed or missing periods block protected financial changes, including pending-deposit cancellation. Do not change historical periods to force a transaction through; use the authorized period-management and correction process.

data.name: UserGuide_ResidentAdminLoginStep
data.value: Residents and building administrators: sign in with the registered mobile number and your personal PIN.

data.name: UserGuide_SuperAdminLoginStep
data.value: SuperAdmin: use the approved email address and password, then complete two-factor verification if prompted.

data.name: UserGuide_RoleContextStep
data.value: If your account has multiple roles or building scopes, choose the context you intend to use. Resident access stays apartment-scoped; building-administrator access stays building-scoped.

data.name: UserGuide_InitialPinStep
data.value: At first sign-in, change the issued PIN when the system asks you to. Never share your PIN or use another person's credentials.

data.name: Reversed_Reversed
data.value: Reversed — a previously posted deposit was reversed; the original financial history remains available.
